question: How was cosmic time dilation finally seen in quasars, after a 2010 study had found none?
answer: By treating their flicker as random and fitting it across 190 quasars watched for two decades. Expansion should make events at redshift 4 look five times slower, as it already does for distant supernovae. Lewis and Brewer found exactly that stretch in 2023: seen from here, the young universe runs in slow motion.
move: Finding nothing may only mean the clock was too noisy to read.
reference: Lewis & Brewer, Detection of the cosmological time dilation of high-redshift quasars, Nature Astronomy 7, 1265, 2023
